fieldMapping.note: Stripe session id used as Idempotency-Key for HubSpot request

assumptions: The Stripe webhook payload includes a customer.email field and a session id.
The HubSpot contact is identified and updated/created by the email property.
The integration can pass the Stripe session id as the Idempotency-Key header when calling HubSpot's API.

notes: Stripe webhooks are authenticated via signature verification (Stripe-Signature header); the connector must validate the signature using the endpoint secret.
The webhook payload is sent as a JSON object with top-level fields: id, type, data.object containing the session details.
The customer email is located at data.object.customer.email.
The Stripe session ID is the top-level id field.
Ensure the endpoint is configured to receive checkout.session.completed events in the Stripe Dashboard.
Stripe recommends verifying webhook signatures to prevent spoofing.
The contact_email path parameter must be URL-encoded if it contains special characters.
The properties array accepts objects with property and value fields; only email is required for identification, but other properties can be included.
If a contact with the given email exists, it is updated; otherwise, a new contact is created.
The response includes vid (HubSpot internal ID) and isNew boolean indicating whether a new contact was created.
This endpoint is part of the legacy v1 Contacts API; HubSpot recommends using v3 (/crm/v3/objects/contacts) for new integrations, but v1 createOrUpdate is still supported.
No pagination applies as this is a single contact create/update operation.
